name: Serengeti National Park
description: Experience the Great Migration, sweeping savannah sunsets, and year-round predator action in one of Africa's most iconic safari landscapes.
shortDescription: Migration drama, classic safaris, and huge wildlife density.
visaNotes: Visa on arrival or e-visa depending on nationality.

name: Masai Mara National Reserve
description: Kenya's flagship safari reserve, known for big cats, dramatic river crossings, and high-end camp experiences.
shortDescription: Big cats, migration crossings, and premium safari camps.
visaNotes: Electronic travel authorisation required for many visitors.

name: Victoria Falls
description: A thunderous natural wonder pairing waterfall viewpoints, helicopter rides, rafting, and sunset cruises.
shortDescription: Epic waterfall power with adventure and river sunsets.
visaNotes: KAZA UniVisa can simplify travel across Zimbabwe and Zambia for eligible travelers.

name: Sossusvlei
description: Towering dunes, surreal desert textures, and one of Africa's most photogenic sunrise landscapes.
shortDescription: Red dunes, sunrise climbs, and minimalist desert beauty.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many nationalities; always verify latest immigration rules.

name: Cape Town
description: A city where mountains, beaches, wine country, and design-forward urban experiences meet.
shortDescription: Atlantic beaches, Table Mountain, food, and city energy.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many travelers for tourism stays.

name: Marrakech
description: A vibrant cultural destination with riads, souks, gardens, architecture, and easy access to the Atlas Mountains.
shortDescription: Colorful medina life, design hotels, food, and culture.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many tourism markets for shorter stays.

name: Zanzibar Archipelago
description: Beach escape meets Swahili heritage, reef adventures, spice farms, and boutique island stays.
shortDescription: Beaches, Stone Town, spice trails, and warm Indian Ocean water.
visaNotes: Same Tanzanian visa regime as the mainland.

name: Ngorongoro Crater
description: An ancient caldera delivering concentrated wildlife sightings, crater-rim scenery, and a strong Big Five appeal.
shortDescription: A natural amphitheater with dense wildlife and dramatic scenery.
visaNotes: Falls under Tanzania visa rules.

name: Seychelles
description: A jewel-like Indian Ocean archipelago of 115 islands, renowned for granite boulder beaches, turquoise lagoons, coral reefs, and exceptional luxury resorts.
shortDescription: Granite boulders, turquoise lagoons, and barefoot luxury.
visaNotes: All nationalities receive a free visitor's permit on arrival for up to 30 days.

name: Mauritius
description: A stunning volcanic island in the Indian Ocean offering emerald lagoons, world-class golf, luxury beach resorts, and a rich multicultural heritage.
shortDescription: Lagoon beaches, luxury resorts, and vibrant Creole culture.
visaNotes: Visa-free for most nationalities for stays up to 90 days.

name: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park
description: An ancient, mist-covered rainforest in southwestern Uganda sheltering nearly half the world's remaining mountain gorillas, alongside Batwa forest-people heritage and extraordinary biodiversity.
shortDescription: Mountain gorilla trekking in Uganda's misty rainforest.
visaNotes: Uganda e-visa required (~USD 50); apply online before travel — no visa on arrival. Gorilla permits are separate: USD 800/person in peak season (USD 600 in the Apr/May/Nov low season), booked via the Uganda Wildlife Authority. Daily permits are capped, so book 3-6+ months ahead.

name: Amboseli National Park
description: Famous for free-roaming elephant herds photographed against the snow-capped backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro, Amboseli delivers one of Africa's most iconic safari images.
shortDescription: Elephant herds beneath Kilimanjaro's snowy peak.
visaNotes: ETA required for all visitors; no visa on arrival. USD 30 standard fee via the official etakenya.go.ke portal only. East Africa Tourist Visa (USD 100) also valid here.

name: Avenue of the Baobabs
description: A surreal dirt road near Morondava lined with centuries-old baobab trees rising over 30 meters, best experienced at golden-hour sunset when the silhouettes turn deep amber against the sky.
shortDescription: Centuries-old baobab giants, best at golden-hour sunset.
visaNotes: Visa on arrival for most nationalities; 15 days fee-free, 30 days USD 35-37, longer stays up to USD 67. Yellow Fever certificate only required if arriving from an endemic country.

name: Skeleton Coast
description: A remote, fog-shrouded stretch of Atlantic coastline scattered with century-old shipwrecks, vast seal colonies, and desert-adapted wildlife where the dunes meet the cold Benguela current.
shortDescription: Shipwrecks, seal colonies, and fog where desert meets ocean.
visaNotes: Since April 2025, Namibia requires a visa for US/UK/EU nationals (previously visa-free). Visa on arrival costs NAD 1,600 (~USD 85); default stay 30 days, extendable. Apply online in advance via eservices.mhaiss.gov.na.

name: Fish River Canyon
description: The second-largest canyon in the world, carved over 500 million years, offering dramatic viewpoints and a legendary 5-day wilderness hiking trail down to the Ai-Ais hot springs.
shortDescription: The world's second-largest canyon and its famous 5-day trail.
visaNotes: Since April 2025, Namibia requires a visa for US/UK/EU nationals. NAD 1,600 (~USD 85) on arrival or pre-applied online; default stay 30 days. The multi-day hiking trail is officially open only 1 May–15 September due to extreme heat.

name: Lake Nakuru National Park
description: A walled sanctuary protecting one of Kenya's most important black and white rhino populations, alongside flamingo-lined shores and dramatic cliff viewpoints overlooking the soda lake.
shortDescription: Rhino sanctuary and flamingo shoreline near Nakuru town.

topExperiences.title: Black & White Rhino Sanctuary
topExperiences.subtitle: One of Kenya's Best Rhino Spots

visaNotes: ETA required for all visitors. USD 30 via the official etakenya.go.ke portal only.

name: Diani Beach
description: Kenya's premier coastline south of Mombasa: powder-white sand, a fringing coral reef, and consistent trade winds that make it one of East Africa's top kitesurfing destinations.
shortDescription: Powder-white sand, coral reefs, and East Africa's top kitesurfing.
visaNotes: ETA required. USD 30 via the official etakenya.go.ke portal only.

name: Lake Malawi
description: Africa's third-largest lake, a freshwater inland sea ringed by sandy beaches and home to more fish species than any other lake on Earth, best explored from the laid-back shores of Cape Maclear.
shortDescription: Africa's freshwater 'sea' of beaches and rainbow cichlids.
visaNotes: US and UK nationals are visa-free for up to 30 days; extension possible in-country.

name: Simien Mountains National Park
description: A dramatic UNESCO World Heritage highland of jagged escarpments and deep gorges, home to troops of endemic Gelada baboons and the trek up Ras Dashen, Ethiopia's highest peak.
shortDescription: Jagged highland escarpments and endemic Gelada baboon troops.
visaNotes: E-visa required (official evisa.gov.et only — avoid lookalike sites). 30-day single-entry is USD 82; a 90-day single-entry option is USD 202. Visa on arrival also available at Addis Ababa Bole Airport.

name: Blyde River Canyon
description: One of the world's largest 'green' canyons, anchoring South Africa's scenic Panorama Route with the iconic Three Rondavels, Bourke's Luck Potholes, and sweeping views over the Lowveld, often combined with a Kruger safari.
shortDescription: The Panorama Route's green canyon and Three Rondavels view.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many travelers; standard South Africa entry rules apply. Often combined with a Kruger National Park safari itinerary.

name: Dakar & Gorée Island
description: A dynamic West African capital where vibrant street art, Afrobeat rhythms, and Teranga hospitality fuse with the haunting history of Gorée Island's UNESCO-listed slave house.
shortDescription: West African culture, music, and poignant colonial history.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many nationalities for up to 90 days.

name: Etosha National Park
description: A vast salt pan safari destination in Namibia where elephants, lions, rhinos, and hundreds of bird species converge at floodlit waterholes for dramatic night and day wildlife encounters.
shortDescription: Salt pan wildlife watching, floodlit waterholes, and big game.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many nationalities; always verify latest Namibia immigration rules.

name: Kruger National Park
description: One of Africa's largest game reserves, Kruger offers self-drive and guided safari experiences, a guaranteed Big Five sighting, and a wide range of accommodation from bush camps to ultra-luxury lodges.
shortDescription: Big Five safaris, self-drives, and world-class bush lodges.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many travelers; South Africa visa rules apply.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: Africa's highest peak and the world's tallest freestanding mountain. Trekkers of varying fitness levels ascend through five distinct ecological zones to reach Uhuru Peak at 5,895 m.
shortDescription: Africa's roof — a bucket-list trek through five climate zones.
visaNotes: Standard Tanzanian visa rules apply.

name: Volcanoes National Park
description: Home to over a third of the world's mountain gorillas, this Rwandan park offers profoundly intimate wildlife encounters in misty Virunga volcano forests, paired with golden monkey tracking and cultural experiences.
shortDescription: Mountain gorilla trekking in Rwanda's misty Virunga volcanoes.
visaNotes: Rwanda offers visa-free entry to all African Union members and many other nationalities.

name: Sahara Desert
description: The world's largest hot desert stretching across 11 countries, offering camel treks through golden dunes of Erg Chebbi, stargazing under unpolluted skies, and authentic Berber camp experiences.
shortDescription: Camel treks, towering dunes, and a billion stars at night.
visaNotes: Visa requirements vary by country of entry; Morocco is visa-free for most nationalities.

name: Fez
description: Morocco's spiritual and intellectual capital, home to the world's oldest university and the largest living medieval city. The 9th-century medina of Fes el-Bali is a sensory maze of tanneries, madrasas, and artisan workshops.
shortDescription: Medieval medina, ancient tanneries, and Moroccan craftsmanship.
visaNotes: Visa-free for most nationalities for stays up to 90 days.

name: Okavango Delta
description: The world's largest inland delta, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where floodwaters transform the Kalahari into an extraordinary ecosystem teeming with elephants, hippos, leopards, and wild dogs, best explored by mokoro canoe.
shortDescription: Mokoro canoes, floodplain wildlife, and wild dog country.
visaNotes: Visa-free for most nationalities for stays up to 90 days.

name: Luxor
description: The world's greatest open-air museum, where the Valley of the Kings, Karnak Temple, and Luxor Temple sit along the Nile, offering an unmatched concentration of pharaonic monuments.
shortDescription: Valley of the Kings, Karnak Temple, and Nile felucca cruises.
visaNotes: E-visa or visa on arrival available for most nationalities.

name: Pyramids of Giza
description: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world. The Great Pyramid of Khufu, the Sphinx, and the Giza Necropolis deliver an incomparable encounter with human civilisation's most ambitious construction.
shortDescription: The last ancient wonder — pyramids, Sphinx, and desert mystique.
visaNotes: E-visa or visa on arrival available for most nationalities.

name: Chefchaouen
description: The 'Blue Pearl' of Morocco, a mountain medina of infinite blue-washed lanes, artisan shops, and Rif Mountain hikes that has become one of Africa's most Instagrammed destinations.
shortDescription: Blue-washed medina lanes, mountain air, and artisan markets.
visaNotes: Visa-free for most nationalities for stays up to 90 days.

name: Bazaruto Archipelago
description: A remote Indian Ocean archipelago of five pristine islands in Mozambique, protecting the last viable population of dugongs in East Africa and offering world-class diving, flamingo dunes, and exclusive island lodges.
shortDescription: Dugong sanctuary, flamingo dunes, and untouched Indian Ocean reef.
visaNotes: Visa on arrival available at Mozambique entry points for most nationalities.

name: Ouidah & Pendjari National Park
description: A dual experience combining Ouidah's living Voodoo culture and slave-trade heritage on the Slave Route with Pendjari's remote safari ecosystem, home to one of West Africa's last significant populations of lions, elephants, and hippos.
shortDescription: Voodoo heritage meets West Africa's wildest safari ecosystem.
visaNotes: E-visa required for most visitors; apply online before travel.

name: Meroë Pyramids
description: The forgotten pyramids of the ancient Kushite Kingdom, more numerous than Egypt's, rising steeply from red desert dunes near the Nile. Virtually crowd-free, they offer a profound off-the-beaten-path encounter with African antiquity.
shortDescription: More pyramids than Egypt, in the Sudanese desert, crowd-free.
visaNotes: Sudan requires a visa for most nationalities; check current situation before travel.

name: Tsingy de Bemaraha
description: A UNESCO World Heritage wilderness of razor-sharp limestone pinnacles in western Madagascar, accessible only by suspension bridges and via ferrata, sheltering unique lemur species and endemic flora found nowhere else on Earth.
shortDescription: Razor-sharp limestone labyrinths, lemurs, and Malagasy wilderness.
visaNotes: Tourist visa on arrival available for most nationalities at Madagascar entry points.

name: Abu Simbel Temples
description: Two colossal rock temples built by Ramses II, relocated stone-by-stone to save them from the rising Nile. The four 20-meter seated statues guarding the entrance are among antiquity's most awe-inspiring sights.
shortDescription: Ramses II's monumental temples carved from a mountainside.
visaNotes: Same Egyptian visa regime as Luxor and Giza.

name: Lalibela Rock Churches
description: Eleven medieval monolithic churches carved downward from solid red volcanic rock in the 12th century, connected by tunnels and trenches. A living pilgrimage site and one of Africa's most extraordinary architectural achievements.
shortDescription: Eleven churches carved from solid rock, still in worship today.
visaNotes: Same Ethiopian e-visa as Simien Mountains.

name: Chobe National Park
description: Botswana's first national park, home to the largest elephant concentration on Earth. The Chobe Riverfront delivers exceptional boat-based wildlife viewing, while the Savuti region is famous for lion and leopard drama.
shortDescription: Elephant capital of Africa with riverfront game viewing.
visaNotes: Visa-free for most nationalities for stays up to 90 days.

name: South Luangwa National Park
description: The birthplace of the walking safari and Zambia's premier wildlife reserve. The Luangwa River sustains enormous hippo and crocodile populations, while the valley is considered one of Africa's best leopard-viewing destinations.
shortDescription: Walking safari birthplace and Africa's leopard capital.

topExperiences.title: Walking Safari
topExperiences.subtitle: On Foot in Big Game Country

visaNotes: Visa on arrival for most nationalities; KAZA UniVisa also valid.

name: Cape Coast & Elmina Castles
description: Two UNESCO World Heritage castles on Ghana's coast, central to the transatlantic slave trade. The 'Door of No Return' at Cape Coast Castle is one of the most emotionally powerful historical sites in Africa.
shortDescription: UNESCO slave-trade heritage forts on Ghana's Gold Coast.

topExperiences.title: Elmina Castle
topExperiences.subtitle: Oldest European Building in Sub-Saharan Africa

visaNotes: Visa-free for many nationalities including US, UK, and EU citizens.

name: Virunga National Park
description: Africa's oldest national park, home to mountain gorillas, active volcanoes, and the world's largest lava lake at Nyiragongo. The most biodiverse protected area on the continent, though travel requires careful planning.
shortDescription: Gorillas, active volcanoes, and the world's largest lava lake.
visaNotes: DRC visa required; park-arranged visa letters simplify the process. Check current security situation before booking.

name: Comoros Islands
description: The 'Perfume Isles' — a volcanic archipelago between Mozambique and Madagascar with ylang-ylang plantations, active volcanoes, world-class diving, and virtually no tourist crowds.
shortDescription: Volcanic 'Perfume Isles' with world-class diving, crowd-free.
visaNotes: Visa on arrival at all entry points for most nationalities.

name: Réunion Island
description: A French overseas department in the Indian Ocean featuring Piton de la Fournaise, one of Earth's most active volcanoes, plus the Cirques of Mafate, Salazie, and Cilaos — dramatic calderas accessible only by foot or helicopter.
shortDescription: Active volcano, epic cirque hiking, and French-Creole culture.

topExperiences.title: Piton de la Fournaise
topExperiences.subtitle: One of Earth's Most Active Volcanoes

visaNotes: As a French overseas department, EU/Schengen rules apply. Many nationalities visa-free.

name: São Tomé & Príncipe
description: The 'African Galápagos' — two tiny volcanic islands straddling the equator with endemic birds, jungle-covered volcanic plugs, cacao plantations, and empty beaches. Africa's second-smallest country and one of its best-kept secrets.
shortDescription: Jungle volcanoes, endemic wildlife, and empty equatorial beaches.
visaNotes: Visa on arrival for most nationalities; e-visa also available.

name: Tunis & Carthage
description: The ancient medina of Tunis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, paired with the ruins of Carthage — the Phoenician city-state that rivaled Rome — and the blue-and-white village of Sidi Bou Said.
shortDescription: Phoenician ruins, Ottoman medina, and blue-and-white coastal charm.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many nationalities including EU, UK, and US for up to 90 days.

name: Jinja & Source of the Nile
description: The adventure capital of East Africa, where the White Nile explodes out of Lake Victoria. World-class white-water rafting, bungee jumping, and river cruises at the exact spot where the world's longest river begins.
shortDescription: White-water rafting where the Nile begins its 6,650 km journey.
visaNotes: Same Ugandan e-visa as Bwindi.

name: Gondar & Fasil Ghebbi
description: The 'Camelot of Africa' — a 17th-century royal enclosure of castles and palaces in the Ethiopian highlands, plus the stunning Debre Berhan Selassie church with its iconic angel-covered ceiling.
shortDescription: Ethiopia's 'Camelot' — castles, palaces, and angel-painted church.
visaNotes: Same Ethiopian e-visa as Simien Mountains and Lalibela.

name: Saloum Delta
description: A UNESCO World Heritage delta of mangroves, islands, and bolongs (branches) where the Saloum River meets the Atlantic. Home to abundant birdlife, shellfish islands, and the Serer people's distinctive culture.
shortDescription: Mangrove labyrinth, bird paradise, and Serer culture.
visaNotes: Visa-free for many nationalities for up to 90 days.

name: Lake Kivu
description: One of Africa's Great Lakes, ringed by emerald hills and resort towns. The perfect post-gorilla-trek relaxation spot with kayaking, island hopping, and lakeside dining in Gisenyi (Rubavu).
shortDescription: Rwanda's Great Lake — kayaking, islands, and lakeside chill.
visaNotes: Rwanda side visa-free for many nationalities; DRC side requires visa.

name: Erg Chigaga Dunes
description: Morocco's wildest and most remote Saharan dune field, accessible only by 4x4 or camel from M'Hamid. Larger and less crowded than Erg Chebbi, with true wilderness camping under billion-star skies.
shortDescription: Morocco's most remote Saharan dunes, far from the crowds.
visaNotes: Visa-free for most nationalities for stays up to 90 days.
